chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ali ibn Ismail Al-Mithammi, from Abdul-A'la, the slave of the family of Saam, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is the meaning of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Inna ma na'uddu lahum 'adddan' (We only number out to them a number)?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'What is it (meaning) with you?' I said, 'The number of the days.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The fathers and the mothers are counting that. No, but it is the number of the breaths.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'We only number out to them a number' mean in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the common assumption that the 'numbering' in Quran 19:84 refers merely to the duration of days, instead identifying it as the precise counting of breaths (*anfas*). This interpretation highlights the meticulous nature of divine accounting in Shia theology, emphasizing that every moment of life is individually recorded and weighed. The narration underscores the transition from a general chronological view to a granular, spiritual assessment of human existence.
